guideposts.label: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 5 of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: A second opportunity for the sprinters? After Tadej Pogacar’s historic solo victory in Andorra la Vella, La Vuelta 26 is in Catalunya with a mostly flat stage from Falset to Roquetes, from Costa Daurada to Terres de l’Ebre (173,3km). The route features 1,662 metres of elevation with a single categorised climb: Puerto de Paüls (cat. 3), to be summited as the race enters the final 25 kilometres. Spr

guideposts.label: La Vuelta 26 is in Spain
guideposts.detail: After Monaco, France and Andorra, La Vuelta settles in Spain, the fourth country on this edition’s route. The race visited four countries last year too: Italy, France, Andorra, and Spain.

guideposts.label: New stage towns
guideposts.detail: Falset and Roquetes both make their first appearance as stage towns of La Vuelta. The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Herman

guideposts.label: Falset and the iconic Poblet
guideposts.detail: Falset was a stage town on day 3 of the 1960 Volta a Catalunya. Born that year, team Ferrys won the TTT (stage 3a) with their emblematic leader Miguel Poblet. The Catalan icon won the race for the second time that year. He won 33 stages of the Volta, and also 3 in La Vuelta, 3 in the Tour de France, 20 in the Giro d’Italia, 2 Milano-Sanremo…

guideposts.label: Uijtdebroeks won't start today
guideposts.detail: After finishing last yesterday in Andorra, Cian Uijtdebroeks won't start stage 5, Movistar announced: "Following further tests and examinations, it has been determined that the injury sustained in his crash during the 2nd stage is more extensive than initially estimated."

guideposts.label: White jersey
guideposts.detail: Second of the young riders standings of the Tour de France 2025, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) leads this specific classification for the first time in a Grand Tour after his strong performance in Andorra. Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) trails by 21’’ and Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) by 59’’.

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Tadej Pogacar (winner), but also Jay Vine (11th) and Pablo Torres (14th), UAE Emirates XRG had the best collective performance in Andorra. They increase their lead in the team standings with a gap of 6’20’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike and 10’26’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike.

guideposts.label: A battle through the wind?
guideposts.detail: Terres de l'Ebre is a wind exposed area that could favour echelons as recently demonstrated in stage 5 of the 2025 Volta a Catalunya (Paüls > Amposta), won by Matthew Brennan. Today’s forecast calls for southeast winds of 20 km/h. guideposts.label: The start is slightly delayed
guideposts.detail: The race direction is waiting for a rider who had a mechanical during the parade. Radio Vuelta just announced the start will be given after they exit Capçanes (at km 2.5 on today's route).

guideposts.label: A gap of 10 seconds at km 11
guideposts.detail: Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) is likely hoping for some support to build today's breakaway on demanding roads.

guideposts.label: The first attacks of the day
The gap is still increasing: 2'20''
guideposts.detail: Which teams will react? None of the attacker represent a GC threat but there are real powerhouses to try andflip the script en route to Roquetes.

guideposts.label: The pedigree of the leaders
guideposts.detail: Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma), Walter Calzoni (Pinarello-Q36.5) and Mattia Gaffuri (Picnic PostNL) are not only competing in their first La Vuelta, but also their first Grand Tour! Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility) has one Giro d’Italia under his belt, and he made a name for himself by winning the 15th stage last May, holding off the peloton in Milan. guideposts.label: Gap under control?
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach km 26 with a gap of 2'14''.

guideposts.label: 4 leaders at km 29 (+2'05'')
guideposts.detail: Stefan Küng (Tudor) is no longer part of the front group.

guideposts.label: Küng is caught by the bunch
The gap keeps decreasing
guideposts.detail: The peloton only trail by 1'16'' at km 35. Isit a sign of the tension in the bunch on a wind exposed course?

guideposts.label: Gaffuri, from the amateur rainbow jersey to La Vuelta
guideposts.detail: At 27 years old, Mattia Gaffuri (Picnic PostNL) participates in his first La Vuelta, in his first professional season. The Italian rider is a former runner, who turned to cycling after injuries. Unfortunately, his development coincided with the Covid-19 pandemics, preventing him from taking the decisive steps to the professional peloton despite a consuming desire to race on the road. guideposts.label: 4 Catalan riders in the peloton, including Spain's national champion
guideposts.detail: There are 4 Catalan riders in the peloton: David de la Cruz (Sabadell), Marcel Camprubi (Barcelona), Paul Miquel (Sant Quirze del Vallès), and MarcBrustenga (Santa Eulàlia de Ronçana). Last June, Camprubi was the 14th Catalan rider to win the men’s Elite road race of the Spanish national championship, following in the footsteps of Joaquim Rodriguez (2007).
